tfResources.role: primary/sole mapping — CfnHttpNamespaceProps maps 1:1 to ServiceDiscoveryHttpNamespaceConfig; no nested/standalone sub-resources exist in this Cfn resource (unlike PrivateDnsNamespace/PublicDnsNamespace which embed vpc/HTTP properties or route53 objects), so only one TF resource is needed.

attributeNotes:
CfnHttpNamespaceProps has exactly 3 props: description (optional string), name (required string), tags (optional Array<cdk.CfnTag>). All three map cleanly:
- description -> description (same semantics, optional string, no unit/shape mismatch)
- name -> name (required string, same semantics)
- tags (Array<{key,value}> CfnTag list) -> tags ({[key:string]: string} map). This is a SHAPE mismatch: Cfn uses a list-of-key/value-object form (CloudFormation tag list), TF uses a flat string-keyed map. Conversion requires transforming Array<CfnTag> into a Record<string,string> (drop duplicate keys, no order preservation needed since TF tags are unordered).
No unmappable Cfn props were found — all 3 props have direct TF equivalents.
Read-only/generated attrs: Cfn attrArn (Arn) / attrId (Id) correspond to TF computed `arn` and `id` attributes on ServiceDiscoveryHttpNamespace (id is the namespace id, arn is the namespace ARN). TF also exposes a computed `httpName` getter (fully-qualified HTTP name) that has no Cfn counterpart (informational only, not something that needs mapping from Cfn props).
TF Config additionally exposes `id` (optional/computed passthrough), `region`, and `tagsAll` (tags merged with provider default_tags) which have no Cfn equivalent — these are TF-provider-specific additions with no CFN prop counterpart, safe to leave unset/default during conversion.
No units/casing concerns beyond the tags shape (CfnTag {key,value} camelCase objects vs TF map<string,string>); `name`/`description` are plain strings in both with no casing translation needed.

cfnResource: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Instance (CfnInstance / CfnInstanceProps) — instantiated identically by all four L2 constructs (AliasTargetInstance, CnameInstance, IpInstance, NonIpInstance) in aws-servicediscovery v2.233.0. Each construct only differs in how it populates the `instanceAttributes` map before creating a single `new CfnInstance(this, 'Resource', { instanceAttributes, instanceId, serviceId })`.

tfResources.role: primary — 1:1 flat mapping. CfnInstance has exactly 3 CFN props (instanceAttributes, instanceId?, serviceId), which correspond directly to TF's attributes, instance_id, service_id. There are no nested Cfn sub-properties that split off into separate standalone TF resources for this resource — all four L2 constructs (AliasTargetInstance, CnameInstance, IpInstance, NonIpInstance) resolve to this single TF resource, differing only in the contents of the `attributes`/`instanceAttributes` map they populate.

attributeNotes:
instanceAttributes (CfnInstanceProps, type `any | IResolvable`, REQUIRED — non-optional in CFN) -> attributes (TF, `{ [key: string]: string }`, required, non-optional). Type-strictness nuance: CFN types the value as free-form `any | IResolvable` while TF strictly types it as a string-valued map; every CDK L2 here already inserts only string values (e.g. port.toString()), so no shape conflict at synth time. No unmappable props here — the free-form map of magic string keys (AWS_INSTANCE_IPV4, AWS_INSTANCE_IPV6, AWS_INSTANCE_PORT, AWS_INSTANCE_CNAME, AWS_ALIAS_DNS_NAME, AWS_EC2_INSTANCE_ID, AWS_INIT_HEALTH_STATUS, plus arbitrary customAttributes) passes through verbatim key/value on both sides — CFN and TF both just accept a string map, so no key renaming is needed inside the map itself.

instanceId (CfnInstanceProps, optional string) -> instance_id (TF, REQUIRED string). Cast/shape mismatch: CFN allows omitting instanceId, but every CDK L2 construct here always supplies `props.instanceId || this.uniqueInstanceId()` (IpInstance, CnameInstance, NonIpInstance) or `props.instanceId || Names.uniqueId(this)` (AliasTargetInstance), so the generated CFN template always has a concrete value. TF marks it required with no default, matching actual runtime behavior — handling: always populate from the L2's computed instanceId (never leave undefined) when generating TF config.

serviceId (CfnInstanceProps, required ARN|string) -> service_id (TF, required string). Direct 1:1, both take `props.service.serviceId`. No shape mismatch (CFN doc notes it can be an ID or ARN for shared namespaces — TF field is a plain string with the same semantics).

TF-only extra fields with no Cfn counterpart: `id` (optional, TF-provider-SDK legacy import-id override — leave unset in generated config, do not conflate with CFN logical/physical id) and `region` (optional, standard AWS provider multi-region override — leave unset unless the stack targets a non-default provider region).

L2-level (non-Cfn) props consumed before reaching CfnInstance and therefore having NO corresponding Cfn/TF prop at all: BaseInstanceProps.customAttributes (spread `...props.customAttributes` into instanceAttributes at synth time, not a separate field), IpInstanceBaseProps.port/ipv4/ipv6 (validated then folded into AWS_INSTANCE_PORT/AWS_INSTANCE_IPV4/AWS_INSTANCE_IPV6 keys of instanceAttributes; port defaults to 80 when omitted), CnameInstanceBaseProps.instanceCname (folded into AWS_INSTANCE_CNAME), AliasTargetInstanceProps.dnsName (folded into AWS_ALIAS_DNS_NAME), and every construct's `service: IService` (resolved to serviceId, and also used purely client-side for validation — e.g. checking dnsRecordType/routingPolicy/namespace type/discoveryType — with no CFN/TF representation). NonIpInstance additionally requires at least one customAttributes entry (client-side validation only). When mapping, translate these L2 props into entries of the TF `attributes` map exactly as CDK does client-side, not into separate TF resource attributes.

Casing: CFN uses camelCase (instanceAttributes, instanceId, serviceId); TF/CDKTF uses snake_case for scalar fields (instance_id, service_id) but the `attributes` map itself keeps its CFN-defined UPPER_SNAKE key names (AWS_INSTANCE_IPV4 etc.) unchanged — those are AWS Cloud Map protocol constants, not CDK-casing artifacts, and must NOT be re-cased.

No unit mismatches: port is stringified in both worlds (CDK does `port.toString()` before inserting into instanceAttributes — confirmed in ip-instance.js; TF's attributes map is also string-valued), so no numeric-vs-string conversion is needed at the TF layer beyond what CDK already does.

tfResources.role: Primary (sole) mapping. Covers name, vpc, description, tags 1:1. Exposes computed attrs arn, hosted_zone, id matching CfnPrivateDnsNamespace.attrArn / attrHostedZoneId / attrId. No nested Cfn prop in this resource rises to the level of a separate standalone TF resource (unlike e.g. Service's DnsConfig -> Route53 records), so this is a ONE-TO-ONE mapping, not one-to-many.

attributeNotes:
Field-by-field mapping (CfnPrivateDnsNamespaceProps -> ServiceDiscoveryPrivateDnsNamespaceConfig), verified against servicediscovery.generated.d.ts lines 379-414 and service-discovery-private-dns-namespace/index.d.ts lines 7-45:
- description (string, optional) -> description (string, optional). Direct match.
- name (string, required) -> name (string, required). Direct match.
- vpc (string, required) -> vpc (string, required). Direct match (both take the VPC ID string).
- tags (Array<cdk.CfnTag> i.e. [{key,value}] list, optional) -> tags (Record<string,string> map, optional). SHAPE MISMATCH: Cfn tags is a list-of-key/value-object; TF tags is a plain string map. Must transform [{key,value}] -> {[key]: value} during conversion. TF also auto-manages tagsAll (tags + provider default_tags) which has no Cfn equivalent — leave unset/computed.
- properties (IResolvable | CfnPrivateDnsNamespace.PropertiesProperty, optional), specifically the nested chain properties.dnsProperties.soa.ttl (number, SOA negative-caching TTL) -> UNMAPPABLE. The aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace TF resource exposes no argument for SOA/TTL or any 'properties'/'dnsProperties' block at all (confirmed absent from ServiceDiscoveryPrivateDnsNamespaceConfig, lines 7-45 — only description/id/name/region/tags/tags_all/vpc present). Handling: drop this prop during conversion and flag/warn; there is no TF-side workaround for setting the SOA TTL on this resource (it's fixed to the Route53-managed default). If the TTL value truly must be controlled, that would require an out-of-band Route53 SOA record modification, which is outside the scope of this Cfn resource's 1:1 TF equivalent.
- Read-only/computed attributes: attrArn -> `arn` (computed), attrHostedZoneId -> `hosted_zone` (computed, note CASING/NAME mismatch: HostedZoneId (Cfn) vs hosted_zone / camelCase `hostedZone` accessor in TF construct), attrId -> `id` (computed). No unit/casing mismatch beyond naming style (Cfn PascalCase attribute name vs TF snake_case/camelCase getter).
- TF-only arguments with no Cfn equivalent (leave unset during conversion): `region` (optional; the AWS region to manage the resource in — in Cfn this is implicit from the stack/deployment context, not a resource prop) and `id` (optional settable input in addition to being the computed identifier; SDKv2 legacy field, normally left computed).
- No other candidate directories from `service-discovery-*` apply to this Cfn resource: service-discovery-public-dns-namespace and service-discovery-http-namespace correspond to the sibling Cfn resources CfnPublicDnsNamespace/CfnHttpNamespace, not this one; service-discovery-service/instance and the data-aws-service-discovery-* data sources are unrelated (they back CfnService/CfnInstance or are read-only lookups).

cfnResource: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PublicDnsNamespace (CfnPublicDnsNamespace, from aws-cdk-lib/aws-servicediscovery, used by the L2 PublicDnsNamespace construct in public-dns-namespace.ts)

tfResources.role: Primary and only mapping - direct 1:1 equivalent of AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PublicDnsNamespace. CfnPublicDnsNamespaceProps.description -> description, .name -> name, .tags (CfnTag[]) -> tags (map<string,string>). Computed attrs: attrArn -> arn, attrId -> id (TF resource id), attrHostedZoneId -> hosted_zone (TS getter `hostedZone`).

attributeNotes:
Direct/simple mappings:
- description (Cfn) -> description (TF, optional string) - direct.
- name (Cfn, required) -> name (TF, required) - direct.
- tags (Cfn: Array<CfnTag> i.e. [{Key,Value}]; note the class also exposes a TagManager `tags` and raw `tagsRaw`) -> tags (TF: {[key:string]: string} flat map) - shape/casing mismatch: array-of-objects vs plain map, keys lowercase in TF attribute name but tag key strings themselves preserve case.
- attrArn -> arn (computed) - direct, same semantic value, casing lower in TF (`arn` vs `Arn`).
- attrId -> id (computed, TF resource id doubles as the namespace id) - direct but note TF exposes it as the generic Terraform `id` rather than a distinctly named attribute.
- attrHostedZoneId -> hostedZone getter / `hosted_zone` HCL attribute (computed) - direct value equivalence but name mismatch: CFN "HostedZoneId" vs TF "hosted_zone"/"hostedZone" (no trailing "Id").

Unmappable / lossy props:
- properties (PropertiesProperty) -> properties.dnsProperties (PublicDnsPropertiesMutableProperty) -> soa (SOAProperty) -> ttl: number. This entire nested chain (Properties.DnsProperties.SOA.TTL, the SOA record TTL for the Route 53 hosted zone created by the namespace) has NO equivalent field on aws_service_discovery_public_dns_namespace - the TF AWS provider (v6.52.0) does not expose SOA/TTL configuration for this resource at all (verified against index.d.ts: only description, id, name, region, tags, tags_all are configurable; computed arn/hosted_zone). Handling: this prop must be dropped/unmapped during conversion; if the CFN template sets a non-default SOA TTL it cannot be reproduced via this TF resource - would need to be flagged as unsupported (there's also no separate/nested TF resource that covers it since the hosted zone is AWS Cloud Map-managed, so this is a case of an unmappable Cfn prop rather than a case needing an additional TF resource).

TF-only extras (no Cfn source):
- region (TF only) - optional per-resource region override, not present in Cfn model (Cfn/CloudFormation region is stack-level only). Not part of the mapping, just a TF provider addition; leave at default/unset when converting.
- tags_all (TF only, computed) - merged provider-default + resource tags; no Cfn equivalent, purely a TF provider convenience attribute, not something to map from Cfn.

Overall: this is a clean 1:1 Cfn-resource-to-TF-resource mapping (no nested Cfn sub-structs correspond to separate standalone TF resources) except for the one lossy SOA TTL leaf noted above.

cfnResource: CfnService (aws-cdk-lib/aws-servicediscovery, CfnServiceProps) — the CloudFormation-backed resource underlying the aws-servicediscovery v2.233.0 `Service` L2 construct in service.ts. Cfn type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Service.

tfResources.role: Sole/primary mapping — 1:1 resource-level equivalent of CfnService. All of CfnService's nested Cfn property types (DnsConfigProperty, DnsRecordProperty, HealthCheckConfigProperty, HealthCheckCustomConfigProperty) are represented as inline nested blocks on this single TF resource (ServiceDiscoveryServiceDnsConfig/DnsConfigDnsRecords/HealthCheckConfig/HealthCheckCustomConfig) rather than as separate standalone TF resources, so no additional TF resources are needed. Note: the namespace itself (referenced via namespaceId) is a separate upstream resource — aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace / aws_service_discovery_public_dns_namespace / aws_service_discovery_http_namespace — but that is a distinct Cfn resource (CfnPrivateDnsNamespace/CfnPublicDnsNamespace/CfnHttpNamespace), not part of CfnService itself, so it is not counted as part of this one-to-many mapping.

attributeNotes:
Confirmed via /Users/vincentsmet/tcons/conversion-run/cdklib/node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/aws-servicediscovery/lib/servicediscovery.generated.d.ts (CfnServiceProps lines 925-992 + CfnService.{DnsConfigProperty,DnsRecordProperty,HealthCheckConfigProperty,HealthCheckCustomConfigProperty} lines 726-916) against /Users/vincentsmet/tcons/base-servicediscovery/node_modules/@cdktn/provider-aws/lib/service-discovery-service/index.d.ts (ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig lines 7-71 + nested Dns/HealthCheck types lines 72-222). Every CfnServiceProps field (description, dnsConfig, healthCheckConfig, healthCheckCustomConfig, name, namespaceId, serviceAttributes, tags, type) accounted for; oneToMany:false and single-TF-resource mapping verified correct.

Direct field matches: description, namespaceId (top-level), type, dnsConfig.{dnsRecords[].ttl, dnsRecords[].type, routingPolicy}, healthCheckConfig.{failureThreshold, resourcePath, type}, healthCheckCustomConfig.failureThreshold — all map 1:1 with camelCase name equality on the CDKTN side (TF snake_case: description, namespace_id, type, dns_config.{dns_records[].ttl,type, routing_policy}, health_check_config.{failure_threshold, resource_path, type}, health_check_custom_config.failure_threshold).

Unmappable Cfn prop:
- serviceAttributes (CfnServiceProps.serviceAttributes?: any) — no corresponding field anywhere on aws_service_discovery_service in terraform-provider-aws (checked provider-aws version vendored under base-servicediscovery; grep for "serviceattribute"/"service_attribute" across the lib returned nothing). AWS Cloud Map service attributes (PutServiceAttributes/GetServiceAttributes API) are not exposed by this TF resource. Handling: drop/no-op with a warning comment in generated code, or note as a known gap requiring a provider-level custom resource / null_resource + aws cli/lambda workaround if attribute support is required.

Shape/casing/unit + optional-vs-required mismatches:
- name (CORRECTION — mismatch the original mapping missed): CfnServiceProps.name is OPTIONAL (readonly name?: string, generated.d.ts line 961) but TF ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.name is REQUIRED (readonly name: string, index.d.ts line 26). CloudFormation auto-generates a service name when omitted; TF requires one. If the Cfn template omits name, the generated TF config MUST backfill/synthesize a name (e.g. from the construct id or a deterministic token) to satisfy the TF schema's required field — directly analogous to the dnsConfig.namespaceId and healthCheckConfig.type optional/required deltas below. When name IS set it maps 1:1 (camelCase name equality; TF snake_case: name).
- tags: Cfn CfnServiceProps.tags is Array<cdk.CfnTag> (list of {key, value} objects); TF ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.tags is a plain map {[key: string]: string}. Requires a list-of-{key,value}-objects -> map<string,string> conversion during property mapping (also note TF exposes both `tags` and computed `tagsAll`).
- dnsConfig.namespaceId: optional in Cfn's DnsConfigProperty (readonly namespaceId?: string; CFN docs even say it's legacy — "Use NamespaceId in Service instead") but REQUIRED in TF's ServiceDiscoveryServiceDnsConfig (readonly namespaceId: string, index.d.ts line 122). If the Cfn template only sets the top-level CfnServiceProps.namespaceId and omits DnsConfigProperty.namespaceId, the generated TF config must backfill dns_config.namespace_id from the top-level namespaceId to satisfy the TF schema's required field.
- healthCheckConfig.type: required in Cfn's HealthCheckConfigProperty (readonly type: string) but optional in TF's ServiceDiscoveryServiceHealthCheckConfig (readonly type?: string) — safe pass-through, no special handling needed (required->optional is non-breaking).

TF-only fields (additions on the TF side, not mapping gaps):
- forceDestroy: ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.forceDestroy?: boolean — no Cfn/CfnServiceProps counterpart; should default to false/undefined to preserve CloudFormation's non-destructive delete semantics as closely as possible.
- region: ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.region?: string (index.d.ts line 36) — TF provider-level per-resource region override with no Cfn counterpart (Cfn region is stack/deployment-scoped); leave unset to inherit provider config.
- id: ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.id?: string — TF SDKv2 auto-added identity field; not a Cfn prop.
- tagsAll: computed TF-only tag rollup (provider default_tags + resource tags).

Attribute/Ref translation (handled at L2 layer, not Config props):
- CfnService exposes Ref/GetAtt attrs (Arn, Id, InstanceCount, Name) via CfnService class properties; TF resource exposes a computed `arn` getter and the TF resource's synthesized `id` doubles as the CloudMap service ID — map attrArn -> arn, ref/attrId -> id. attrInstanceCount has no direct TF attribute equivalent and would require a data source or be dropped.
- No unit differences found for ttl/failureThreshold (both plain numeric seconds/count in both models).
